From shadowboxing Parisians to chihuahuas fronting rap videos, the acceleration in generative AI capability is now impossible to miss on our feeds. 

This week, Matt and Marianna explain how new software allows users to 'reskin' video content to make anyone say or do literally anything they like.

They discuss the resulting shift from realism to absurdism online, the existential threat to any type of IP ownership, and why independent creators inevitably suffer the most.

Katie Zacharia is "transitioning out" of her role as White House press secretary, the White House has confirmed to the BBC.
 
They did not provide a timeline for when she would be leaving the position.
 
US President Donald Trump earlier said he told Zacharia to “reconsider” her role.
 
He said he told her, “You don’t have to do this”, after her debut in the briefing room earlier this week.
 
Zacharia has been treated “very, very badly” by the media in recent days, Trump told reporters outside the White House.

author: BBC News
description:
Protesters and anti-riot police have clashed in Albania's main cities in scenes not witnessed for decades.
 
Government buildings have been attacked, as have some private businesses.
 
The country's capital Tirana has seen months of protests from an anti-government "Flamingo" movement, but the clashes have now spread to the main cities of Durrës, Shkodër, Lezhë and Vlora in the west, Gjirokastër in the south and Korçë in the east.
 
The new demonstrations were announced as a student movement, ostensibly demanding action by the government to help with the high cost of education fees and books - and the higher cost of living.

description:
There have been sobering  warnings this week from MI5, the UK's AI Minister and a number of security officials - AI is already a threat to our lives. 

But despite those fears, innovation and AI development continues at breakneck speed. 

So this week on AI Decoded we focus in on that central question of AI - should we accelerate the development of ever more powerful AI systems, or slow down before the risks become unmanageable?

It's the question at the centre of a major new film, Artificial, which explores the growing divide between OpenAI co-founders Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever over the answer. 

To discuss it all, Marc Cieslak and Dr Stephanie Hare are joined by technology futurist Bernard Marr and AI safety researcher Roman Yampolskiy, one of the world's leading voices on the risks posed by superintelligent AI.

Russian President Vladimir Putin said Kyiv had also tried to hit refineries on Wednesday - which Ukraine denied - but there had been no "significant damage".

author: BBC News
description:
Is Washington leaving Saudi Arabia to fend for itself?
 
Last week, Houthi rebels launched a series of missile strikes on Riyadh, Saudi Arabia’s capital. Surveillance footage showed a fireball erupting as airport passengers ran for cover. At least fourteen people have been killed and hundreds were injured.
 
The attack is the latest escalation in a decade-long war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in neighbouring Yemen. The Saudis have long relied on financial, military and intelligence support from the United States, particularly in their fight against the Houthis.  But Washington so far has shown little appetite for direct involvement in the fighting.
 
So why is the United States holding back? And what does that mean for the people caught in the middle?
 
The BBC’s chief international investigations correspondent, Nawal Al-Maghafi, recently reported from inside Yemen and joins The Global Story’s Asma Khalid to discuss why this conflict is escalating and what might happen next.
title: Why Trump isn’t going to war with the Houthis | BBC News

description:
Four people, including a teacher and children aged 5, 8 and 11, have been killed in a shooting at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon, local police say.
 
The suspected attacker, a 16-year-old boy, forced his way into the school by firing at locked doors. He was also killed in the shooting.
 
Emergency services in the city of Bend responded after receiving a call that an armed person had fired at a car before he was seen going into the Silver Rail Elementary School with a long gun.
 
The suspect was shot dead by an armed member of the community who followed the suspect inside the school, police say.
